K9 Bone Sweep Tool -- DEV SERVER ONLY.
/k9bonetool goto <index>  -- preview one exact index (marker + on-screen label)
/k9bonetool next [step]   -- step the preview forward (default 1)
/k9bonetool prev [step]   -- step the preview backward (default 1)
/k9bonetool known         -- list candidate indices from known bone names (still verify with goto)
/k9bonetool test          -- really attach a marker prop at the current preview index
/k9bonetool stop          -- stop the preview and remove any test prop

tablet.help_tab_shop_desc: Everything about the K9 supply shop, in two sections: where its ped stands in the world for each department, and what it sells -- at what price, and which certification tier is required to buy each item. You may see only one of the two sections: they are separate permissions, so someone can be trusted with the catalog without being trusted to move the shop, or the other way round.
tablet.help_tab_catalogs_desc: The three lists this resource lets you edit yourself, in one place: certification tiers (like Trainee, Certified, Senior, and which extra abilities each unlocks), permission keys (the named capabilities you can grant one specific person), and XP ranks (how much XP each rank needs, on both the K9 and handler ladders). Open it before certifying anyone if the default tiers do not match how your server is organised, or when a permission you want to grant does not exist yet. You may see fewer than three sections: permission keys and XP ranks each disappear when their own feature is switched off.

tablet.k9_profiles_intro: Hand-tune one dog's sprint speed, scent range, medkit cooldown, and stamina drain rate beyond what its handler's XP rank already gives it, without moving the whole rank.
tablet.k9_profiles_empty: No K9 currently has a hand-tuned override.
tablet.k9_profile_not_yet_live_hint: Changes here take effect the next time this K9's rank is recalculated -- earning XP, the handler reconnecting, or a server restart -- not necessarily this instant if the K9 is already active right now.
tablet.k9_profile_speed_multiplier_hint: Multiplies this K9's movement and sprint speed. Must be greater than 0 -- there is no fixed upper limit here; an extremely high value may still be refused if it exceeds what your server allows. Default: 1.0, meaning no change from its rank.
tablet.k9_profile_speed_clamp_note: This value genuinely applies in-game, all the way up to your server's speed ceiling -- that is Config.MaxSpeedScentMultiplier in config.lua, 10 by default, which is also the highest the game engine itself accepts. There is no hidden lower cap. This note used to say the opposite, and it was right at the time: anything above 2x saved, showed here, and silently never happened. That is fixed.
tablet.k9_profile_scent_range_multiplier_hint: Multiplies how far this K9 can pick up a scent trail or search target. Must be greater than 0 -- there is no fixed upper limit here; an extremely high value may still be refused if it exceeds what your server allows. Default: 1.0, meaning no change from its rank.
tablet.k9_profile_medkit_cooldown_multiplier_hi: Multiplies the wait time between medkit uses on this K9 -- a SMALLER number means a SHORTER wait. Range: above 0 up to 1.0 (1.0 = no change; this can only shorten the cooldown, never lengthen it). Default: whatever its rank already gives it.
tablet.k9_profile_note_hint: A short, plain-text reason for this override, visible to any high-command officer who looks this K9 up later. Up to 120 characters, no special formatting characters.
tablet.k9_profile_blank_means_no_override_place: Leave blank to keep the current value
tablet.k9_profile_field_clear_hint: Leaving a field blank leaves it exactly as it already was -- it does not clear it. To remove every override on this K9 at once, use Reset All Overrides below; there is no way to clear a single field on its own.

tablet.cmdref_k9sit_does: Commands your K9 to sit in place.
tablet.cmdref_k9bark_needs: K9 access, and Basic Bark Sounds enabled on this server.
tablet.cmdref_k9scentvision_does: Toggles Scent Vision: coloured dots on the ground showing where nearby people recently walked. Each dot fades on its own timer, so a longer trail means someone passed more recently.
tablet.cmdref_k9scentvision_needs: K9 access, and Scent Vision enabled on this server.
tablet.cmdref_k9bitehold_does: Toggles Bite & Hold on the nearest eligible target, or releases it if your K9 is already holding one.
tablet.cmdref_k9bitehold_needs: K9 access, and Bite & Hold enabled on this server.
tablet.cmdref_k9takedown_does: Attempts a non-lethal takedown on the nearest fleeing eligible target.
tablet.cmdref_k9takedown_needs: K9 access, and Non-Lethal Takedown enabled on this server.
tablet.cmdref_k9dragtoggle_does: Toggles dragging the nearest downed target, or releases it if your K9 is already dragging one.
tablet.cmdref_k9dragtoggle_needs: K9 access, and Prop Dragging enabled on this server.
tablet.cmdref_k9leash_does: Attaches a leash to the nearest eligible player, or detaches your current leash if you already have one.
tablet.cmdref_k9leash_needs: K9 access to attach a leash to someone. Detaching is always available, with no certification needed. Leash Mechanics must be turned on for your server.
tablet.cmdref_k9vehicle_does: Gets your K9 into the nearest K9 vehicle's free seat, or gets it back out if it is already riding in one.
tablet.cmdref_k9vehicle_needs: K9 access to get in. Getting out is always available. Vehicle Entry/Exit must be turned on for your server.
tablet.cmdref_k9partner_does: Sends a Partner Up request to the nearest eligible player, or breaks your current partnership if you already have one.
tablet.cmdref_k9partner_needs: K9 access to send a Partner Up request. Breaking a partnership is always available, even right after a reconnect. Handler Partnership must be turned on for your server.
tablet.cmdref_k9gear_does: Opens your own K9 gear stash.
tablet.cmdref_k9gear_needs: An active K9 certification, and you must currently be controlling your K9. This feature must be turned on for your server.
tablet.cmdref_k9treat_does: Treats the nearest eligible K9 using a medkit from your own inventory.
tablet.cmdref_k9treat_needs: Your job must be permitted to use K9 medkits (not K9 access or certification of your own), and on some servers an individual grant for this feature too. You must be holding the item this server has configured as a K9 medkit, and there must be an eligible K9 nearby. This feature must be turned on for your server.
tablet.cmdref_k9deploykennel_does: Places a portable kennel at your feet.
tablet.cmdref_k9deploykennel_needs: An active K9 certification, and you must currently be controlling your K9. This feature must be turned on for your server.
tablet.cmdref_k9exitkennel_does: Gets you out of a kennel you are resting in.
tablet.cmdref_k9exitkennel_needs: Nothing -- always available while resting in a kennel, so you can never get stuck inside one.
tablet.cmdref_k9kennel_does: Deploys, enters, or exits your kennel -- whichever one makes sense right now. Old names /k9deploykennel and /k9exitkennel still work too.
tablet.cmdref_k9kennel_needs: An active K9 certification, and you must currently be controlling your K9, to deploy or enter. Exiting is always available. This feature must be turned on for your server.
tablet.cmdref_k9debug_does: Writes a diagnostic report about your own K9 state to a file inside the script folder, for you to hand to a developer. Nothing is printed to the console.
tablet.cmdref_k9debug_needs: Your server owner must switch this on first (Config.DebugDump.enabled). It reports only on you -- never on anyone else.
tablet.progression_intro: Your rank on each ladder. The K9 ladder is earned by working as the dog; the handler ladder is earned by working with one. They advance separately, and your server can run either without the other.
tablet.progression_k9_off: This server does not track K9 XP, so there is no rank to show here.
tablet.progression_handler_off: This server does not track handler XP, so there is no rank to show here.
tablet.progression_top_rank: You are at the top of this ladder.
tablet.cmdref_k9dog_does: Shows or changes whether a character is permanently pinned as a K9. One command for both: /k9setdog and /k9removedog still work too.
tablet.cmdref_k9propattach_does: Attaches or removes a prop (for example a vest) on your K9.
tablet.cmdref_k9propattach_needs: An active K9 certification, and you must currently be controlling your K9. This feature must be turned on for your server.
tablet.cmdref_k9throwfetchball_does: Throws a fetch ball for your K9 to chase.
tablet.cmdref_k9throwfetchball_needs: An active K9 certification. Only one ball may be in play for you at a time. This feature must be turned on for your server.
tablet.cmdref_k9dropfetchball_does: Drops the fetch ball you are currently carrying.
tablet.cmdref_k9dropfetchball_needs: Nothing -- always available while you are carrying a ball, so you can never get stuck holding one.
tablet.cmdref_k9recallfetchball_does: Cancels your own fetch throw in progress.
tablet.cmdref_k9recallfetchball_needs: Nothing -- always available, so a throw can always be called off.
tablet.cmdref_k9fetch_does: Throws, recalls, or drops the fetch ball -- whichever one makes sense right now. Old names /k9throwfetchball, /k9recallfetchball and /k9dropfetchball still work too.
tablet.cmdref_k9fetch_needs: An active K9 certification to throw. Recalling or dropping is always available. Only one ball may be in play for you at a time. This feature must be turned on for your server.
tablet.cmdref_k9stats_does: Shows the server's K9 XP leaderboard.
tablet.cmdref_k9stats_needs: An active K9 certification. This feature must be turned on for your server.
tablet.cmdref_k9certify_does: Makes a handler's certification current for their department -- certifies them if they are new, renews their expiry if they already hold one. Works whether they are online (first form) or offline (second form).
tablet.cmdref_k9certify_needs: High Command, the certify permission, or your department's certifier rank. An ONLINE target must be in a configured department and within certifying distance (unless you are certifying yourself and self-certification is allowed). An OFFLINE target is refused if your server requires an on-model check, since that can only happen while they are online -- use the online form once they log in instead.
tablet.cmdref_k9decertify_does: Revokes a player's current department certification -- works whether they are online (first form) or offline (second form).
tablet.cmdref_k9decertify_needs: Same as /k9certify. Proximity is required for an ONLINE target unless you are revoking your own.
tablet.cmdref_k9settier_does: Changes an actively-certified handler's certification tier -- works whether they are online (first form) or offline (second form).
tablet.cmdref_k9settier_needs: Same as /k9certify. The target must already hold an active certification.
tablet.cmdref_k9specialize_does: Grants an online, actively-certified handler a specialization.
tablet.cmdref_k9specialize_needs: Same as /k9certify. The target's certification tier must be allowed to hold specializations. There is no offline version of this command -- granting a specialization always requires the target to be online.
tablet.cmdref_k9unspecialize_does: Revokes a handler's specialization -- works whether they are online (first form) or offline (second form).
tablet.cmdref_k9givexp_does: Awards XP directly to an online player.
tablet.cmdref_k9givexp_needs: High Command or the grant-XP permission. The amount is capped by this server's configured maximum per grant, and repeated use is rate-limited.
tablet.cmdref_k9bonetool_does: Developer tool for sweeping through a test prop's skeleton bones, to find the right one for attaching a leash, vest, or prop.
tablet.cmdref_k9bonetool_needs: Your department's boss rank or High Command, AND a server operator must have explicitly turned this dev tool on -- it is off by default, and unsafe to leave on in production.
tablet.cmdref_k9permission_does: Grants or revokes a named permission key (a capability like certifying others, or a specific feature/block override) directly to/from a citizen. Old names /k9grantpermission and /k9revokepermission still work too.
tablet.cmdref_k9permission_needs: High Command only. This feature must be turned on for your server. You cannot grant a permission to yourself.
tablet.cmdref_k9grantpermission_needs: High Command only. This feature must be turned on for your server. You cannot grant a permission to yourself.
tablet.cmdref_k9revokepermission_needs: High Command only. This feature must be turned on for your server.
tablet.cmdref_vault_does: Makes your K9 hop over a low obstacle right in front of it, like a fence or a low wall.
tablet.cmdref_vault_needs: K9 access, and Advanced Agility enabled on this server. You must be controlling your K9, and the obstacle has to be low enough to clear.
tablet.cmdref_pursuitsprint_does: Gives your K9 a short burst of real speed so it can catch up with a fleeing suspect it is already chasing.
tablet.cmdref_pursuitsprint_needs: K9 access, and Pursuit Sprint enabled on this server. There must be a fleeing suspect nearby for your K9 to chase.
tablet.cmdref_toggle_camera_does: Switches your view between looking through your K9's own eyes (first-person) and the normal camera behind it (third-person). Press again to switch back.
tablet.cmdref_toggle_camera_needs: You must be controlling your K9. Nothing else -- no certification and no server setting can turn this off.
tablet.cmdref_toggle_camera_feed_does: Opens a small picture-in-picture window showing what your partner (K9 or handler) can currently see. Press again to close it.
tablet.cmdref_toggle_camera_feed_needs: K9 access, an online partner within range, and Partner Camera Feed enabled on this server.
tablet.cmdref_toggle_thermal_vision_does: Turns on heat vision: people and animals glow so they are easier to spot, even in the dark or through smoke. Press again to turn it off. Turning this on switches Night Vision off automatically.
tablet.cmdref_toggle_thermal_vision_needs: You must be controlling your K9, and Thermal Vision enabled on this server. No certification needed.
tablet.cmdref_toggle_night_vision_does: Turns on night vision so you can see clearly in the dark. Press again to turn it off. Turning this on switches Thermal Vision off automatically.
tablet.cmdref_toggle_night_vision_needs: You must be controlling your K9, and Night Vision enabled on this server. No certification needed.
tablet.cmdref_k9vision_does: Cycles your K9 vision: off, then Night Vision, then Thermal Vision, then back off -- skipping whichever of those two your server has turned off. Old names /qbx_k9unit:toggleThermalVision and /qbx_k9unit:toggleNightVision still jump straight to one specific mode, if that's what you want instead.
tablet.cmdref_k9vision_needs: You must be controlling your K9. No certification needed. Does nothing but notify you if both Night Vision and Thermal Vision are turned off on this server.
tablet.help_intro_line1: This page walks you through using the tablet from scratch, in plain language. Just need a quick lookup? The command list at the bottom of this page shows every command with a live yes/no on whether you can use it right now.
tablet.help_role_note_k9: You are seeing the K9 version of this guide because you are currently playing as a dog.
tablet.help_role_note_handler: You are seeing the Handler version of this guide because you are not currently playing as a dog.
tablet.help_role_note_uncertified: You are seeing the Getting Started version of this guide because you do not hold an active certification yet.
tablet.help_role_note_high_command_suffix: Because you are also High Command, the extra admin sections below are showing too.
tablet.help_start_k9_1: 1. You are playing as the dog. A separate player -- your handler -- plays the human half of the team.
tablet.help_start_k9_2: 2. High command makes you the K9 from their tablet: they certify you as a K9 and pick your breed, in one step. From then on you have the role and the dog's body together.
tablet.help_start_k9_3: 3. Check the top of the My Record tab. It shows "Partnered" or "No Partner" -- that tells you whether a handler is currently paired with you.
tablet.help_start_k9_4: 4. If it says "No Partner", wait for a handler to walk up to you and choose "Partner Up" from their interact menu. You will get an accept-or-decline prompt -- accept it.
tablet.help_start_k9_5: 5. Scroll to the command list at the bottom of this page and read "Basic K9 Commands" and "Combat & Restraint" first -- those are your everyday moves and the keys already bound to them. Whatever you have started, you can always stop it with the same key that started it -- letting go is never blocked, even if your certification lapses mid-bite.
tablet.help_start_handler_1: 1. Look at the top of the My Record tab. It shows your name and, right under it, whether you are certified yet.
tablet.help_start_handler_2: 2. If it says you are not certified, find a supervisor -- someone with the right rank in your department, or a High Command officer -- and ask them to certify you. They do this from their own tablet's Command Console tab.
tablet.help_start_handler_3: 3. Once certified, the My Record tab's "Ready to use right now" list shows exactly which abilities you can use today. That list changes as your certification, tier, and server settings change -- check back after anything changes.
tablet.help_start_handler_4: 4. The command list at the bottom of this page shows the exact command and key for everything on that list.
tablet.help_start_handler_5: 5. If you want a K9 partner, find someone playing as a K9 and use "Partner Up" from your interact menu while standing near them. They get an accept-or-decline prompt.
tablet.help_start_handler_6: 6. If you want to become the K9 yourself instead of staying the handler, that is a separate role change -- see "Turn Someone Into a K9" further down this page.
tablet.help_start_high_command_heading: Also: Because You Are High Command
tablet.help_start_high_command_intro: Everything above still applies to you -- High Command is not a separate job, it is a handler or K9 who also has admin tools. Here is where to start with those tools specifically.
tablet.help_start_high_command_1: 1. Open the Command Console tab first and type the person's name, citizen ID or server ID into the one search box -- it searches everyone online and everyone certified at once. Someone offline and never certified? Type their exact citizen ID and press Open. Their whole record opens on one screen: certifications, role, XP, access and abilities, in the order you normally work down them.
tablet.help_start_high_command_2: 2. To set someone up, open them from the Command Console and press Certify under their department. Leave the choice on Handler for a handler, or pick a breed to make them the K9 -- that one press is the whole setup. Tier and specializations are optional extras on the same screen.
tablet.help_start_high_command_3: 3. If you need to know what someone has actually been doing, use the Audit Trail tab -- it is read-only and shows real history, not a guess.
tablet.help_start_high_command_4: 4. Every whole-server setting -- feature switches and their numbers, certification tiers, permission keys, XP ranks, the supply shop and the tablet theme -- is under one tab, Server Settings, one click per section. See "Every Tab, Explained" below for what each section does.
tablet.help_tabs_intro: Only the tabs you can actually use are listed below -- if a tab is not shown here, you cannot see it on your own tablet either.
tablet.help_tab_my_record_desc: Everything about you, in one place, and the first screen you land on: who you are and what to do next, then your certifications, then where you stand on both XP ladders, then every ability with its exact status -- the ones you can use now and the ones you still have to earn.
tablet.help_tab_console_desc: One search box finds anyone: type a name, citizen ID or server ID and it searches everyone online and everyone certified at once (browsing those lists needs the Audit capability or High Command). Press Open to go straight to an exact citizen ID -- that always works, even for someone who has never been certified.
tablet.help_tab_theme_desc: Change the tablet's own colors and title for every player on the server. Open it to re-brand the tablet, not to fix anything broken.
tablet.help_tab_roster_desc: Everyone currently hired, across every configured department, with their callsign, certification tier, XP, and active partner if any. Switch between K9s and Handlers at the top; both share one "Unassigned" section -- certified people who have not been assigned to either roster yet, which is not an error, just people still waiting to be sorted. Open a row to hire, fire, promote, demote, change someone's roster role, or set a callsign -- all from their profile, the same one the Command Console opens.
tablet.help_tab_runtime_control_desc: Turn individual features on or off for the whole server, and adjust the numeric settings behind them, without editing config files or restarting. Open it when a feature needs to change right now, or when you need to know whether one is currently on.
tablet.help_tab_audit_desc: A read-only history of who certified whom, who partnered with whom, who searched whom, XP grants, and department-wide activity. This is privacy-sensitive -- it shows real names and real actions. Open it to investigate something that already happened.
tablet.help_tasks_heading: How to Do the Common Things
tablet.help_task_get_certified_1: 1. Find someone who can certify you: a supervisor at the right rank in your department, or anyone in High Command.
tablet.help_task_get_certified_2: 2. Ask them in person or over the radio -- there is no way to request a certification yourself from the tablet.
tablet.help_task_get_certified_3_template: 3. They open their own tablet's Command Console tab, find your name or citizen ID, open your record, and press {certifyLabel} for your department. You will see the change on your own My Record tab the next time you open it.
tablet.help_task_partner_up_heading: Partner Up With a Handler or K9
tablet.help_task_partner_up_1: 1. Stand close to the other player -- handler or K9, either side can start this.
tablet.help_task_partner_up_2: 2. Open your interact menu on them and choose "Partner Up" -- if you are the K9, your K9 Unit radial menu has the same option.
tablet.help_task_partner_up_3: 3. The other player gets an accept-or-decline prompt. Once they accept, the My Record tab for both of you shows "Partnered" instead of "No Partner".
tablet.help_task_partner_up_4: 4. To split up later, open your K9 Unit radial menu and choose "Break Partnership" -- either side can end it, any time, even if the other player is offline.
tablet.help_task_vehicle_heading: Put Your K9 In the Car
tablet.help_task_vehicle_1: 1. As the K9, walk up to the vehicle your handler is using. Only vehicles set up to carry a K9 will show this option -- ask High Command if you think one is missing it.
tablet.help_task_vehicle_2: 2. Open your interact menu on the vehicle and choose "Get in the Back Seat".
tablet.help_task_vehicle_3: 3. To let your K9 back out, open the interact menu on the vehicle again and choose "Get Out of the Vehicle".
tablet.help_task_search_1: 1. As the K9, walk up to a person or a vehicle.
tablet.help_task_search_2: 2. Open your interact menu and choose "Search Person for Contraband" or "Search Vehicle for Contraband". Your K9 plays a sniffing animation while the server checks the result.
tablet.help_task_search_3: 3. This only works while you are playing as the K9 -- a handler cannot search on the K9's behalf.
tablet.help_task_treat_1: 1. This is not limited to handlers -- anyone whose job is set up for it (usually EMS) can do this, as long as they are carrying a K9 medkit item.
tablet.help_task_treat_2: 2. Walk up to the injured K9 and open your interact menu on them. Choose "Treat This K9's Injuries (Uses a K9 Medkit)".
tablet.help_task_treat_3: 3. The medkit item is used up. If the option is not there at all, either this feature is turned off on this server, or you do not have a K9 medkit.
tablet.help_task_kennel_1: 1. As the K9, open your K9 Unit radial menu and choose "Kennel (Deploy/Enter/Exit)". It is placed on the ground just in front of you.
tablet.help_task_kennel_2: 2. You can only have one active kennel at a time -- pick it back up (walk up to it and use the "Pick Up Kennel" option) before deploying another.
tablet.help_task_kennel_3: 3. Any K9 can use a deployed kennel to rest: walk up to it and choose "Rest in Kennel". Choose "Exit Kennel" (or use its own keybind) to get back out.
tablet.help_task_kennel_4: 4. This same "Kennel (Deploy/Enter/Exit)" option always appears in the radial menu, even when deploying is turned off -- if choosing it does nothing while you have no kennel out, this feature is disabled on this server -- ask High Command.
tablet.help_task_stop_being_k9_1: 1. There is no self-service way to turn yourself back -- and that is deliberate, not a bug. Being the K9 is a role high command puts you in, so high command is who takes you back out of it.
tablet.help_task_stop_being_k9_2: 2. Ask any High Command officer to open their tablet, find you on the Command Console, and press "Revert to Human". It takes them about ten seconds.
tablet.help_task_stop_being_k9_3: 3. It always works. They can do it even if your certification has lapsed, your access was revoked, or you hold no grants at all -- there is no state you can end up in where the button stops working.
tablet.help_task_stop_being_k9_4: 4. Your original appearance was saved when you were turned into the K9, so you get your own character back, not a default one. Logging out and back in does NOT revert you: you stay the K9 across sessions until someone presses that button.
tablet.help_task_scent_vision_1: 1. As the K9, press the "K9: Toggle Scent Vision" key (. -- the full stop -- by default, rebindable in Settings > Key Bindings > FiveM) to show coloured dots marking where nearby people have recently walked. Press it again to turn it off.
tablet.help_task_scent_vision_2: 2. Only a handful of the closest people's trails are shown at once, each its own colour, and the dots fade out and disappear as they get older.
tablet.help_task_scent_vision_3: 3. If pressing the key does nothing, either this feature is turned off on this server, or this server has set it to run for everyone automatically instead of needing the key -- ask High Command.
tablet.help_task_hc_certify_someone_1: 1. Go to the Console tab and type their name, citizen ID or server ID into the search box. Someone brand new who is offline will not be in either list -- type their exact citizen ID and press Open. Most certification actions require the target to be online.
tablet.help_task_hc_certify_someone_2_template: 2. Open their record. Next to {certifyLabel}, leave it on Handler or pick a K9 breed, then press it. Tier and specializations are optional, on the same screen.
tablet.help_task_hc_toggle_feature_heading: Turn a Feature On or Off
tablet.help_task_hc_toggle_feature_1: 1. Open Server Settings, pick Runtime Control, and find the feature by name.
tablet.help_task_hc_toggle_feature_2: 2. Flip its switch. Most features take effect immediately for every player -- but not all of them do. Read the small note under the switch: some only apply after a restart, and a few (protected or not-yet-audited features) cannot be changed from here at all.
tablet.help_task_hc_assign_k9_1: 1. Go to the Command Console tab, find the person, and open their record.
tablet.help_task_hc_assign_k9_2_template: 2. Next to {certifyLabel} under their department, pick their breed instead of Handler and press it -- they are certified and turned into that dog at once. Already certified? Use "{assignLabel}" in the K9 Role section to pick or change their breed.
tablet.help_task_hc_assign_k9_3_template: 3. To undo it, press "{revertLabel}" -- this works even if they hold no certification or access at all, so it is always available as an emergency undo.
tablet.help_task_hc_check_history_2: 2. Pick what you are looking for -- certifications, partnerships, searches, XP grants, or department-wide activity -- and type the citizen ID.
tablet.help_task_hc_check_history_3: 3. This is privacy-sensitive: it shows real names, real actions, and real timestamps. Only use it when you actually need to investigate something.
tablet.help_trouble_intro: Every refusal on this tablet tells you the real reason -- here is what the most common ones actually mean and what to do about them.
tablet.help_trouble_no_k9_access_title: "You cannot use K9 features right now." (a red notification in the game, not on the tablet)
tablet.help_trouble_no_k9_access_body: This means one of two things: you are not currently wearing a K9 model, or you do not hold an active K9 certification (or access grant). Check the My Record tab -- if it does not show you as certified, see "Get Certified" above. If it does, ask a High Command officer to check whether you are actually set as a K9 ("Assign K9 Role" on your record in their Command Console).
tablet.help_trouble_not_certified_body: You do not hold an active certification for whatever this needs. See "Get Certified" above -- ask a supervisor or High Command.
tablet.help_trouble_feature_off_title: "Disabled server-wide" or "This feature is turned off on this server"
tablet.help_trouble_feature_off_body: A High Command officer switched this off for the whole server, from Server Settings (Runtime Control). It can usually be turned back on the same way -- ask them. A small number of features are marked protected or not-yet-audited and genuinely cannot be turned on from the tablet at all; Runtime Control says so directly when that is the case.
tablet.help_trouble_needs_grant_title: "Requires a grant (not granted)" or "Requires higher authorization"
tablet.help_trouble_needs_grant_body: The feature itself is on, and you are certified, but this specific extra permission has not been given to you personally. Only High Command can grant it, from your record in their Command Console (or Server Settings > Catalogs, if the permission itself does not exist yet).
tablet.help_trouble_rate_limited_body: Wait a few seconds and try again. This is a safety limit, not a permission problem -- nobody needs to grant you anything to fix it.
tablet.help_trouble_self_cert_disabled_title: "Self-certification is turned off on this server"
tablet.help_trouble_self_cert_disabled_body: You cannot certify yourself on this server. Ask someone else who can certify -- a supervisor or High Command.
tablet.help_trouble_target_offline_body: The person you are trying to act on needs to be connected to the server. Ask them to log in, then try again.
tablet.help_trouble_insufficient_authorization_: "You are not authorized to do this. You need a High Command grant."
This action is High Command only. If you believe you should have it, ask an existing High Command officer to raise your department rank, or grant you the specific permission it needs.
tablet.help_tab_partnerships_desc: Shows who you are currently partnered with, or that you have no partner right now. If you are High Command, this same tab also lets you look up anyone else's partnership. Open it to check a pairing -- partnering up and breaking up both happen out in the world (interact menu or K9 Unit radial menu), not on this screen.
tablet.home_view_partners_hint: See your current and past partners.
tablet.mutation_error_not_partnered: That citizen is not currently partnered.
tablet.partnerships_admin_none: This citizen has never been partnered.
tablet.partnerships_count_summary_template: You have had {count} partner(s) in total.
tablet.partnerships_feature_disabled: Partnership tracking is turned off on this server.
tablet.partnerships_history_empty: You have never been partnered with anyone.
tablet.partnerships_next_tier_countdown_templat: {days} day(s) until the next tenure milestone
tablet.runtime_lockout_warning_commandtablet_te: Turning off {name} here does nothing by itself -- it only takes effect once you also set it to false in config.lua and restart the server. Once it does take effect, it removes the tablet entirely for EVERYONE, including High Command -- there is then no in-game screen left to turn it back on. RECOVERY: open config.lua, set {name} back to true, and restart this resource.
tablet.runtime_lockout_warning_highcommand_temp: Turning off {name} immediately removes High Command access for EVERY High Command officer on this server -- not just this tablet's High Command screens, but every High Command power across the whole resource (permission grants, XP grants, appearance swaps, and anything else gated behind High Command status), all at once. Nobody can use this screen to turn it back on once it's off, because this screen's own High Command check depends on this same setting. RECOVERY: this change only lasts for the current session -- simply restarting the server, with or without editing config.lua first, puts {name} back to whatever config.lua says on disk. To make the change permanent instead, open config.lua, set {name} to your intended value there, and restart.
tablet.runtime_lockout_warning_permissiongrants: Turning off {name} immediately stops every individually granted permission (k9.access, k9.certify, k9.audit, k9.givexp, k9.runtimecontrol, k9.tablettheme, and any other per-person grant) from working for whoever holds it -- only rank-based access (High Command or the legacy rank gate) keeps working. Nobody can use a granted permission to turn this back on once it's off. RECOVERY: this change only lasts for the current session -- simply restarting the server, with or without editing config.lua first, puts {name} back to whatever config.lua says on disk. To make the change permanent instead, open config.lua, set {name} there, and restart.
tablet.runtime_lockout_warning_runtimefeatureco: Turning off {name} immediately disables every action this screen itself depends on (turning features on or off and adjusting settings, including undoing your own changes) -- nobody can use this screen to turn it back on once it's off. RECOVERY: this change only lasts for the current session -- simply restarting the server, with or without editing config.lua first, puts {name} back to whatever config.lua says on disk.
tablet.runtime_lockout_warning_tablettheming_te: Turning off {name} immediately stops anyone from changing or resetting the tablet's look -- nobody can change or reset it until the server restarts (seeing the current theme still works fine -- this is only about appearance, nothing else is affected). RECOVERY: this change only lasts for the current session -- simply restarting the server, with or without editing config.lua first, puts {name} back to whatever config.lua says on disk.
tablet.runtime_lockout_warning_generic_template: Changing {name} carries a risk of locking you out, but there's no specific warning written for it yet -- only go ahead if you understand exactly what this setting controls and how to recover (usually by editing config.lua and restarting) if something goes wrong.
tablet.runtime_active_usage_warning_kennel_temp: {subject} currently {activity} right now. Disabling {name} will NOT remove them or force an exit -- a K9 already resting can always leave normally, unaffected -- but nobody will be able to deploy, enter, or pick up a kennel until it is turned back on.
tablet.runtime_active_usage_warning_hold_templa: {subject} currently in a {activity} right now. Disabling {name} will NOT end an already-started hold -- automatic release, expiry, and manual release all keep working regardless -- but nobody will be able to start a NEW {activity} until it is turned back on.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_leashmaxdistance: How far a K9 can wander from its handler on the leash before it is pulled back.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_certifyproximitymet: How close a handler and K9 must stand together to run a certification test.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_vehicleinteractmete: How close a handler must be to a vehicle to load or release a K9 from it.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_tracking_scent_sear: How long a handler must wait between scent searches before trying again.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_tracking_scent_rela: How long a handler must wait before the K9 will relay (bark/alert) on a scent find again.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_tracking_scent_maxr: How far away a scent trail can be and still be found by a search.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_tracking_scent_maxa: How long a scent trail stays trackable after it was left before it goes cold.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_tracking_blood_sear: How long a handler must wait between blood-trail searches before trying again.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_tracking_blood_rela: How long a handler must wait before the K9 will relay (bark/alert) on a blood find again.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_tracking_blood_maxr: How far away a blood trail can be and still be found by a search.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_tracking_blood_maxa: How long a blood trail stays trackable after it was left before it goes cold.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_tracking_gunpowder_: How long a handler must wait between gunpowder-residue searches before trying again.
How long a handler must wait before the K9 will relay (bark/alert) on a gunpowder find again.
How far away gunpowder residue can be and still be found by a search.
How long gunpowder residue stays trackable after it was left before it goes cold.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_adminaudit_commandc: How long an admin must wait between running audit-log lookup commands.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_adminaudit_maxresul: The most certification records the audit log will return in a single lookup.
The most partnership records the audit log will return in a single lookup.
The most search-log entries the audit log will return in a single lookup.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_certificationexpiry: How often the server checks certifications for upcoming or passed expiry and sends warnings.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_k9downdispatch_heal: The K9 health value at or below which a "K9 down" alert is dispatched.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_k9downdispatch_mind: How long a K9 must stay at or below the health threshold before a "K9 down" alert is dispatched (avoids false alarms from a brief health dip).
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_k9downdispatch_poll: How often the server checks K9 health to decide whether to dispatch a "K9 down" alert.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_scenttrailhunt_minr: The closest a Scent Trail Hunt's hidden target can be placed from its start point.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_scenttrailhunt_maxr: The furthest a Scent Trail Hunt's hidden target can be placed from its start point.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_scenttrailhunt_arri: How close a K9 must get to the hidden target to complete a Scent Trail Hunt.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_scenttrailhunt_maxh: How long a Scent Trail Hunt stays active before it automatically times out.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_pursuitsprint_reque: How close a handler must be to their K9 to request a Pursuit Sprint speed boost.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_pursuitsprint_speed: How much faster a K9 moves during a Pursuit Sprint boost (1.0 = no change, higher = faster).
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_pursuitsprint_durat: How long a Pursuit Sprint speed boost lasts once granted.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_combat_biteandhold_: How close a K9 must be to a target to start a Bite and Hold.
The longest a Bite and Hold can be held before it automatically releases.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_combat_nonlethaltak: How close a K9 must be to a target to attempt a Non-Lethal Takedown.
How fast a target must be moving for a Non-Lethal Takedown to be allowed (stops a takedown being used on someone standing still).
How far back in time the target's speed is measured over when checking the Non-Lethal Takedown speed requirement.
How long a target stays ragdolled (knocked down) after a successful Non-Lethal Takedown.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_combat_propdragging: How close a K9 must be to a prop to start dragging it.
The furthest total distance a K9 can drag a prop before it is automatically released.
The longest a K9 can drag a prop before it is automatically released.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_partnership_proximi: How close a handler and K9 must stand together to confirm a partnership request.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_partnership_request: How long a partnership request stays open before it expires unanswered.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_partnership_tenureb: How often the server checks partnerships for tenure milestones (rewards for staying partnered a certain length of time).
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_deployablekennel_pl: How far in front of the handler a deployable kennel is placed.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_deployablekennel_pe: How long a kennel placement request stays open before it expires if not confirmed.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_propattachments_tog: How long a handler must wait between attaching or detaching a prop.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_propattachments_pen: How long a pending prop attachment stays open before it expires if not confirmed.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_propattachments_con: How far the handler can move from where they started before a pending prop attachment is cancelled for moving too far.
tablet.runtime_tunable_desc_fetchmechanic_throw: How far in front of the handler a thrown fetch ball spawns.
How high above the handler a thrown fetch ball spawns.
